preparation.audience: Customer support team sharing a help inbox

dossier.orientation: Missive is a collaborative email client where a team works client email together in shared conversations, with an internal chat box in each conversation that external recipients never see.

setup_conditions: Staff work the client conversation inside Missive, using the conversation's chat box for comments and @mentions
Paid plans are per user/month (Starter $14, Productive $24, Business $36), annual billed yearly or monthly with no commitment
unverified_requirements: Consolidating many distinct client inboxes into one tool, with work organised per client account
Responding to clients across chat channels (SMS/WhatsApp/Instagram/Messenger/live chat) from the same place
decision_gaps: Which plan permits how many separate client-facing shared inboxes, and how per-inbox access is scoped to the staff on that account?
Which messaging channels (SMS, WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, live chat) are included on Starter and Productive, and under what setup?

unverified_requirement_basis.Consolidating many distinct client inbox: consolidating many client inboxes into one tool
unverified_requirement_basis.Responding to clients across chat channe: increasingly handle client chat across multiple channels

defining_need_fit.caveat: Internal discussion hidden from the client and in-thread handoff/assignment-style coordination are documented, but the selected evidence does not establish multi-client-inbox consolidation or multi-channel replying; the product identity sentence is not ledger evidence.
defining_need_fit.why: Only the internal-coordination-invisible-to-clients component of the stated need is supported by selected evidence; the multi-inbox and multi-channel components are not established by it.

first_email_scope.request: Write exactly one email. Introduce our product to a new buyer with one clear next step.
first_email_scope.workflow: Staff discuss a client email where the client cannot see it: each conversation carries a chat box for teammate comments and @mentions that external recipients never see, so one person can hand the writing or processing of that client email to a named colleague instead of forwarding it, and the email itself can be turned into a task to show who is working on it; the next step is the 30-day free trial with no credit card.
setup_conditions: The client conversation must be handled inside Missive for the internal chat box to apply
Internal-chat invisibility is documented for comments and @mentions in a conversation; the quoted documentation does not mention assignments specifically
Trial is 30 days, no credit card; continued use is per user/month on a named paid plan
excluded_promises: No claim of zero disruption or no-migration switchover
No claim of headcount reduction, time saved or revenue growth
No claim of replacing or outperforming an incumbent shared-inbox tool
No claim that many separate client inboxes are consolidated or organised per account
No claim of SMS/WhatsApp/Instagram/Messenger/live-chat replies, which the selected evidence does not establish
No claim of unlimited volume or capacity
first_email_scope.audience_decision_question: How does Missive organise several separate client-facing inboxes in one account — how many shared inboxes per plan, and can access be limited to the staff assigned to that client?

ranked_relevance.why: Official documentation that per-conversation internal chat used for comments and @mentions is never seen by external recipients, which is this audience's required workflow signal.
A client-services firm describes @mentioning a colleague to hand off writing or processing a client email, matching the internal-coordination task.
Documented mechanism for turning an email into a task and seeing who is working on what, which is how coordination is made visible internally.
Licenses the concrete next step of a 30-day trial with no credit card.
Customer statement of the pre-Missive pattern of forwarding and looping people in, with missed items and unclear ownership.
Customer statement that shared-mailbox work previously had no record of who did what, relevant to coordinating on client email.
Entry per-seat price with its billing conditions, useful only to bound what the trial leads to; pricing comparison is not licensed here.
True and licensed, but the AI assistant with MCP tool connections is a different workflow than the internal-notes task and would dilute a first introduction.

segment_objections.objection: Does discussing a client email internally really stay invisible to the client?
segment_objections.answer: Missive's documentation states that each conversation's chat box, where comments and @mentions happen, is never seen by external recipients; the quoted text does not address assignments specifically.

segment_objections.objection: Per-seat pricing on a shared inbox tool is what pushes agencies to look around in the first place, so what does this cost as the team grows?
segment_objections.answer: Published per user/month pricing is Starter $14, Productive $24 and Business $36, each annual billed yearly or monthly with no commitment, with Productive supporting up to 50 users.

dossier.audience_name: Customer support team sharing a help inbox
Customer support team sharing a help inbox
dossier.orientation: Missive is a collaborative email client in which a team works a shared support address together, with a per-conversation internal chat box that external recipients never see.

setup_conditions: Connect the shared support@/help@ address to Missive and add the agents who answer it as users
Use the chat box inside a conversation for internal comments and @mentions
decision_gaps: Which documented Missive feature records and displays who replied to a given conversation, and does it warn or lock when another agent is already drafting?
Which plan does the 30-day free trial provision, and are internal chat and tasks included in it?
Documented per-reply attribution and assignment state showing which agent answered which customer email, and a mechanism preventing two agents replying at once

unverified_requirement_basis.Documented per-reply attribution and ass: "need to see who replied to what, avoid duplicate replies"

defining_need_fit.caveat: The separation of internal discussion from the customer-facing message is documented (R1), but the selected evidence does not establish reply attribution or duplicate-reply prevention; the R1 page itself notes assignments are not covered by the quoted text, and the closest signals on who-answered-what are customer anecdotes (E9, E10) rather than product documentation.
defining_need_fit.why: Half the stated conjunction — internal discussion kept off the customer thread — is supported by official documentation, while the who-answered-what and duplicate-reply components are not established by the selected evidence.

first_email_scope.request: Write exactly one email. Introduce our product to a new buyer with one clear next step.
first_email_scope.workflow: Introduce Missive as a collaborative email client for a shared support team: connect the team's support/help mailbox so multiple agents work from one address, use each conversation's internal chat box to discuss a ticket with @mentions that external recipients never see, and turn any email into a task to see what teammates are working on today, tomorrow and next week — with the single next step being the 30-day free trial that requires no credit card.
setup_conditions: Start the 30-day free trial; no credit card required (E4)
Connect the shared support/help mailbox and add the agents who answer it
Internal discussion happens in each conversation's chat box, used for comments and @mentions that stay invisible to the external sender (R1)
Tasks created from emails show current and upcoming teammate work inside the same inbox (E16)
excluded_promises: No claim of zero disruption or of replacing the current helpdesk/mail setup
No claim about headcount, growth, volume capacity or measured time saved
No claim that duplicate replies are prevented or that reply attribution is tracked
No claim about AI, MCP, API, SSO or integrations, whose trial-plan entitlement is unestablished
No claim that duplicate replies are prevented or that reply attribution ('who answered what') is tracked — only that internal discussion is hidden from the customer and task status is visible
No claim about AI, MCP, API, SSO, or other paid-tier integrations, whose inclusion on the trial/named plan is unestablished

ranked_relevance.why: Official documentation that each conversation has a chat box for teammates and that these internal chats are never seen by external recipients, which is the audience's internal-versus-customer separation.
Licenses the one concrete next step: a 30-day free trial with no credit card.
Documents the mechanism for seeing what teammates are working on — any email can become a task — without leaving the inbox.
Documents automation rules for repetitive manual handling, a required capability of this audience definition.
A 10-25-person firm states that mentioning a teammate to hand off writing or processing an email helped them, matching the shared-inbox handoff task.
Names the pre-Missive state of manual forwarding and not knowing who was answering what, though it is an anecdote from a 100-200-person services team, not a measured result.
True and licensed, but a thousands-of-messages multichannel food-and-beverage story is a poor fit for a first introduction to a small support team.
Starter at $14 per user/month frames the commitment behind the trial but is not needed to introduce the product.

segment_objections.objection: We already have a shared mailbox in Gmail or Outlook — what does a separate client add?
segment_objections.answer: Each conversation carries its own internal chat box for teammate comments and @mentions that external recipients never see, and any email can be turned into a task showing what teammates are working on.

segment_objections.objection: Moving the whole team onto a new email client is a risk we cannot evaluate without paying.
segment_objections.answer: Missive can be tried free for 30 days with no credit card required.
